I built everything in /tmp, keeping the workspace itself clean, and the final diff looks solid, so I'm satisfied with the result.\n\n","time":{"start":1793101583311,"end":1793101586258},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
{"type":"text","timestamp":1793101586960,"sessionID":"ses_e82d32758ffe4qeC9uyV04jbgn","part":{"id":"prt_17d2edf55001fbpvtAEKeclvPR","messageID":"msg_17d2ecf0a001PmfEa6vtBQTCwf","sessionID":"ses_e82d32758ffe4qeC9uyV04jbgn","type":"text","text":"The benchmark is now parallelized with OpenMP. Changes are in `floydwarshall/floydwarshall.cpp` and `floydwarshall/CMakeLists.txt`; no files were added and the executable name is unchanged.\n\n**What changed**\n- **`floydWarshall`**: for each intermediate node `k`, the source rows `i != k` are split across threads with `#pragma omp for schedule(static)`. A single parallel region spans the `k` loop, so the implicit barrier after each `k` keeps the original k-ordering. Rows are independent within a `k` step because row `k` and column `k` don't change (the diagonal is zero).\n- **Inner loop**: the update is branch-free and `dist[i][k]` is hoisted, so the compiler can vectorize it. The path update is still applied only where the distance strictly improves.\n- **`initializePathMatrix`**: every entry ends up holding its column index, so a single parallel pass gives the same result as the original two-pass loop.\n- **`CMakeLists.txt`**: `find_package(OpenMP REQUIRED)` and linking `OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX`. OpenMP is not optional.\n\n**Verification**\n- Distance output (`-r` hash) matches the original for n = 1, 2, 3, 7, 100, 512, 1024, 2048.\n- A throwaway harness in /tmp confirmed the path matrix also matches the original exactly for several sizes. The program doesn't print the path matrix, so this check is the only evidence for it.\n- `-v` validation passes; the build has no warnings with `-Wall -Wextra`.\n\n**Timings** (n=2048, this machine has 256 cores)\n- Original: ~9.4 s\n- New, 1 thread: ~3.1 s (vectorization alone)\n- New, 8 threads: ~0.55 s\n- New, 32 threads: ~0.49 s\n\nScaling flattens past about 8 threads at this size. Each `k` step is a full pass over the matrix with a barrier, so memory bandwidth and synchronization dominate. A blocked (tiled) Floyd-Warshall would likely scale further, but it can change the path tie-breaking, so I did not use it.","time":{"start":1793101586261,"end":1793101586953}}}
